name: recovery_key_scan
description: Locate key material a case can use and say where it is, not what it is: BitLocker 48-digit recovery passwords (ASCII and UTF-16LE text) by file, offset, length and a structure check; private-key headers by type (RSA, EC, DSA, OPENSSH, ENCRYPTED, PGP, plain, or 'other': the header's own text is never echoed) and offset; and the names key files and credential stores are saved under (a name is a lead, not a read of the file). No value, fragment, masked shape or digest of a value is ever in the answer or in the files it names, and a path component shaped like a recovery password (a file named after the key) or like any identifier or secret is withheld from every printed path. A heuristic locator, not a verdict: a value is found unless it is glued to more digits ("key_<value>" is found, "<value>7" is not); passes_structure_check means eight groups divisible by 11 (a plausible transcription), not that the value opens any volume; a file is read up to max_bytes_per_file (default 8 MiB, streamed) and coverage lists every file that failed, was skipped (links, special files, a top-level proc, sys or dev), was read only in part or was not started, with the bytes not read. The tool has its own clock (max_seconds, default 480, below the timeout of 600): at it, or on SIGTERM, SIGINT or SIGHUP, it stops reading, finishes its pages, closes the values file and answers once with status partial, naming every file and directory it did not reach (exit 128 + the signal for a signal); the clock is read for every finding, so a file of nothing but findings is cut at it too, and a read that has not returned five seconds after the clock ends the tool with one partial answer (exit 0) (the stop is the clock's, not the work's: the timer stays armed while the answer is sealed, and a page fault or a read that sits in the system cannot be ended until the call returns) (the scan looks for the dash that follows a group, so the limit is a bound on a large tree or slow media, not the usual case). Every answer carries status and status_basis. It is not OCR, does not unpack archives or containers and does not read key stores. SENSITIVE: it reaches secret material, so run it as a job with secret_output: true (the manifest makes every job that sets write_values one). write_values: true (refused outside a job, and in a job whose process lacks SECRET_OUTPUT=1) creates $OUT/recovery-passwords.jsonl, mode 0600, before it scans (a file or link already there is refused by name) and writes the values, and the real paths, to it and nowhere else; with nothing found it stays empty and the answer says written: 0. Withholding is by shape, measured on random draws per shape planted in a member name or path (rates, not guarantees). Printed whole in 0 of 1,000 draws: hexadecimal ids of 16, 32 and 64, numbers of 10 digits or more, recovery passwords written with dashes, spaces, dots, underscores, no separator or one to three of any other characters between the groups (an en dash, a comma, a colon, a pipe, a tab), also when the groups are cut at the separators of the path (123456-123456/123456-...), full-width, split by invisible characters, or with one decimal digit glued to the first or last group, AWS access key ids, password= and api_key: assignments, user-info, 4x4 groups of capitals and digits joined by - or ., letters and digits of 8, 9, 12, 16 or 40 characters that hold a capital, a small letter and a digit, and a full-width id. Printed whole in some draws: uniform draws of letters and digits (every character as likely a capital, a small letter or a digit as any other) of 8 characters about 2.5%, of 9 about 2%, of 12 about 1%, of 16 about 0.6%, of 24 at most 0.1% and of 40 none; random lowercase letters and digits of 8 about 7%, of 12 about 2.4%, of 16 about 0.4%; 24 random letters 1.5% to 2.6%; a 16-character base32 id 2.2% to 3.4% (by alphabet); four groups of four lowercase hexadecimal digits joined by underscores 4% to 9% (by how the draws are made); an id of 12 or 16 characters whose letters are half Cyrillic or Greek look-alikes about 1%. NOT recognised, by design, and printed whole: an identifier of 7 characters or fewer, a number of 9 digits or fewer, a lowercase-only run of up to 22 letters (it reads as a word), an all-capital letters-only run of any length, three groups of four or five capitals and digits joined by - or . (a rule for them would also withhold upper-case constants such as OpenSSL manual page names), a recovery password cut by anything other than a separator or with a letter in it or glued to it (the groups then show), a ten-digit number written 3-3-4, an e-mail-like lowercase string, and a secret of any other shape; a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true. What the rule is given is bounded: a string of more than 4096 characters (as written or after folding), a path of more than 8192, or a string with a / and a run of more than 256 name characters is withheld whole as '<text too long to judge withheld>' and not judged (the slowest string inside the bound that a search found took 0.13 CPU s). The output check, which reads every printed string once more, is narrower than the rule: with the rule removed it replaces recovery passwords (full-width ones too), AWS ids, password= values, PEM headers, user-info, hexadecimal of 16 digits or more and runs of 24 or more characters that flip between letters and digits, and it lets through numbers of 10 to 20 digits, ids of up to 23 characters, some base64 (about one in five of 32 bytes), every recovery password whose groups are joined by anything but a hyphen, underscore, dot, space or nothing, and every recovery password cut over the components of a path (the first layer alone holds those). The rule also changes names that are not secrets: of the file names of a documents tree 6.9% have a part withheld (10-digit timestamps, UUIDs) and 0.6% of its directories, of an application tree 16% and 3.1% (a word with a digit inside, such as libmp3lame, is withheld in part).

path.description: A directory to walk, or a single file to sweep. Links and special files inside it are not followed or read, and are listed

max_bytes_per_file.description: How much of each file to read (default 8388608, at least 1024); reading is streamed, so a larger value costs time, not memory. A file larger than this is listed as partial with the bytes not read

limit.description: Findings, name hints and coverage exceptions shown inline (default 200 each); all of them are counted, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.<list>.all_results

write_values.description: Write each recovery password found to $OUT/recovery-passwords.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job run as secret output (the harness makes a job that sets this one; the tool checks SECRET_OUTPUT=1 in its environment); the file is created first and a file or link already there is refused; the answer never carries a value

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 480, 1 to 540; the manifest's timeout is 600). At it the scan stops, writes what it has and names the files and directories it did not reach; a read that has not returned five seconds later ends the tool with one partial answer
